title: Sayings on Trade and Faith by Umar
summary: Hazrat Umar valued earning a living alongside religious duties.
translation: Reflecting on earning a livelihood and improving one's economic situation, the saying of Hazrat Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) forces one to think about the far-reaching vision of the Companions. Just as they strengthened their faith, they also fortified the means to do so. Hazrat Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) stated that dying while earning on a journey is more beloved to him than dying in jihad (struggle) in the way of Allah. He also remarked that, apart from jihad, he considers no better place for death than engaging in trade and business for his family. He then recited a verse indicating that commerce is mentioned alongside jihad, underscoring its significance. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) was unaware of many hadiths due to his business engagements. He quoted a verse from a poet, saying, 'Indeed, a wealthy brother is esteemed,' highlighting that earning and eating provide strength for worship. When questioned by someone about the best deed after faith, Hazrat Abu Dharr Ghaffari (may Allah be pleased with him) replied, 'Prayer and eating bread.' Upon receiving a surprised look, he explained that without sustenance, worship cannot be performed, as it strengthens one. Thus, just as one should be strong in worship, the means to do so should also be strong. Similarly, as faith should be strong, the means to strengthen faith should also be robust. May Allah grant us the correct understanding and consciousness of religion, enabling us to succeed both materially and spiritually.
